ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In an electric field, a charged particle with a charge of $-2\!\times\!10^{-9}\mathrm{C}$ is moved from point A to point B, with the work done by the electrostatic force being $-2\times 10^{-7}\mathbf{J}$. Subsequently, the same particle is moved from point B to point C, and the work done by the electrostatic force is $6\times 10^{-7}\mathbf{J}$.

1. Determine the electric potential difference between points A and B, between points B and C, and between points A and C.
2. If the electric potential at point A is defined to be zero, calculate the electric potential energy of the particle at point C.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In an electric field, a charged particle with a charge of $-2\!\times\!10^{-9}\mathrm{C}$ is moved from point A to point B, with the work done by the electrostatic force being $-2\times 10^{-7}\mathbf{J}$. Subsequently, the same particle is moved from point B to point C, and the work done by the electrostatic force is $6\times 10^{-7}\mathbf{J}$. 1. Determine the electric potential difference between points A and B, between points B and C, and between points A and C. 2. If the electric potential at point A is defined to be zero, calculate the electric potential energy of the particle at point C.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Read the given values: q = -2×10^-9 C, W_AB = -2×10^-7 J, and W_BC = 6×10^-7 J. Use the electrostatic work relation W = q(V_initial - V_final). For A to B: V_A - V_B = W_AB/q = (-2×10^-7)/(-2×10^-9) = 100 V. For B to C: V_B - V_C = W_BC/q = (6×10^-7)/(-2×10^-9) = -300 V. Then V_A - V_C = (V_A - V_B) + (V_B - V_C) = 100 + (-300) = -200 V. If V_A = 0, then V_A - V_C = -200 gives V_C = 200 V. The potential energy at C is U_C = qV_C = (-2×10^-9)(200) = -4×10^-7 J.
